title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering during regional failover
author: Priya Menon
description: Summary: Fixes a race and ordering bug in the SLO enforcer backoff + regional failover path that could cause cascading load-shedding and thrashing during partial regional outages. Root cause: when a region hits the SLO enforcer threshold we asynchronously trigger backoff and regional failover; under high concurrency the ordering between marking nodes as 'draining' and updating routing tables could be inverted, causing a short period where requests were simultaneously shed and re-routed back into the affected region. This amplified load and caused the enforcer to oscillate (load-shed->recover->load-shed).  What I changed: 1) enforce a strict sequential transition in the enforcer state machine: set backoff timer -> mark region draining -> publish routing delta -> ack before returning success. 2) added an idempotent compare-and-swap on routing delta application to prevent stale updates from reverting state. 3) tuned backoff smoothing to add a jitter floor to avoid synchronization between regions. 4) added a short grace window to avoid immediate re-admission of traffic while downstream caches and prefix-KV states flush.  Testing: - Unit tests for state transitions and CAS behavior added. - Deterministic integration test that simulates concurrent failover and validates no oscillation across 1k simulated clients. - Stress e2e in perf-lab for 60m showed no SLO enforcer thrash and 42% fewer dropped requests versus baseline.  Rollback plan: revert the deployment of the hotfix rollout (k8s deployment) which will immediately return to previous ordering semantics; additionally we can toggle slo-enforcer.feature_flags.ordering_strict=false in runtime config if a fast soft rollback is required.  Notes: This is a hotfix targeted at production and backported to the 2026-02 release branch. See linked Linear tasks for monitoring and post-incident postmortem.
